title: Usage Insights — Historical Backfill Plan (Route + Model breakdown)
content:
Doc goal
Define what historical data we can backfill for the Usage Insights feature (route + model breakdown), given telemetry/billing retention, instrumentation rollout timing, and data residency constraints. This includes:
- backfill scope options + recommended default
- incremental recompute strategy (safe to run, low warehouse cost)
- correctness/reconciliation plan vs billing totals
- customer-facing expectations + comms (beta/GA)

Owner / decision makers
- Primary: Nadia Rahman (cost attribution)
- Data platform: Logan Wright
- Observability quality: Allison Grant + Caleb Johnson
- Billing totals: Cole Summers
- Console surfacing (banners / messaging): Chloe Martin + Dylan Brooks

Definitions (for this doc)
- “Raw metering events”: request-level usage events produced by gateway/runtime and ingested into telemetry warehouse.
- “Aggregated dataset”: pre-aggregated table used by console queries (by workspace/project, time bucket, route_template, model_bucket, and additional dims).
- “Backfill”: recomputing aggregated dataset for a past time window, using already-retained raw events.
- “Effective backfill coverage”: the oldest date for which we can produce route+model numbers that are both (a) reasonably complete and (b) reconcile to billing within tolerance.

Why backfill is non-trivial
1) Instrumentation availability: route tags and stable model bucketing were not reliably present prior to the instrumentation rollout (ENG-3822 / ENG-3823). Even if raw usage exists, the dimensions needed for insights may be missing or inconsistent.
2) Retention: telemetry raw events and billing ledgers have different retention/availability windows. Backfilling beyond raw telemetry retention is not possible without alternative sources.
3) Attribution semantics changed: route normalization rules (templating dynamic segments) and model alias/version bucketing can change results across time if applied retroactively.
4) Data residency: for Private / certain regulated workspaces, historical raw events may be stored in region-specific partitions with stricter access controls.

Current state (as of 2026-02-10)
- Route tag coverage:
  - Hosted API: good coverage for /v1/chat/completions and /v1/embeddings; known gap previously observed for some streaming emitters in one region (tracked in data quality thread + dashboards).
  - OpenAI-compat endpoints: mapping depends on route normalization library adoption at emitters (see route normalization PR and follow-ups).
- Model bucketing coverage:
  - Model aliases exist in the catalog; bucketing should produce stable “model_family + version” but older events may only have raw model_id.
- Billing reconciliation:
  - Reconciliation suite exists (ENG-3817) but tolerances and rounding rules still being tuned for long time ranges.

Non-goals
- We are NOT attempting to reconstruct missing route tags from logs.
- We are NOT building a one-off per-customer custom backfill pipeline in beta.
- We are NOT guaranteeing a single historical cutoff date for all deployment modes/regions (we will publish a conservative default and caveats).

Constraints & assumptions
Telemetry retention (working assumptions; verify with Security/Compliance doc and actual warehouse TTLs)
- Raw metering events: 30 days retained for interactive analytics use; older data may exist in cold storage but not queryable at acceptable cost/latency.
- Aggregated datasets: 90 days retained (configurable) with low-cardinality dimensions.
Billing ledger availability
- Billing totals per workspace/day are available for at least 12 months (finance reporting needs), but may not include route/model dimensions.
Data freshness / late events
- Late events can arrive up to 48 hours after timestamp (p99), with occasional longer tails during incidents.
- Backfill jobs must be idempotent and handle late arrivals for a bounded “correction window.”

Backfill scope options
Option A — No backfill (forward-only)
- What: start producing insights from the date route/model fields are guaranteed.
- Pros: simplest; avoids misleading historical charts.
- Cons: customers expect “last 7/30 days” immediately; weak adoption; support load (“why is my history empty?”).

Option B — Conservative backfill (recommended for beta)
- What: backfill the last 14 days (rolling) for all hosted workspaces; longer windows only where we can prove dimension completeness and reconcile.
- Pros: covers common “what changed week-over-week” use case; reduces risk of partial/inaccurate numbers.
- Cons: may feel short for FinOps; some customers want 30–90 days.

Option C — Standard backfill (recommended for GA if quality holds)
- What: backfill last 30 days for hosted workspaces; keep correcting the last 7 days daily to account for late events.
- Pros: matches typical console time range defaults; best balance.
- Cons: higher warehouse cost; more chances of historical drift if normalization changes.

Option D — Extended backfill (enterprise ask; not default)
- What: backfill 90 days for select allowlisted workspaces only.
- Pros: supports quarterly chargeback and QBR workflows.
- Cons: cost + operational risk; likely to expose older instrumentation gaps; may require per-workspace exceptions.

Decision proposal
- Beta default: Option B (14 days) for hosted.
- GA target: Option C (30 days) if reconciliation drift and missing-dim rates stay under thresholds for 2+ weeks.
- Extended (90 days): by request, only after validation on that workspace (and only if raw events retained + dims complete).

Backfill strategy (incremental recompute)
High-level approach
- Aggregate is keyed by: workspace_id, project_id, env, deployment_mode, region, time_bucket (hour/day), route_template, model_bucket.
- Backfill job recomputes aggregates for a bounded time window using raw metering events filtered by event_timestamp.
- Writes are performed via partition overwrite (preferred) or merge/upsert keyed on the full dimension set.

Recommended schedule
1) Hourly forward aggregation (normal operation)
- Compute latest hour(s) and update today’s partitions.

2) Daily correction for late arrivals
- Recompute the last 2 days (48h) once per day (e.g., 03:00 UTC) to fold in late events.
- This is NOT “backfill,” but it ensures stability.

3) Historical backfill bootstrap (one-time per rollout)
- When enabling the feature for a workspace allowlist, run a one-time job for the backfill window (14d beta / 30d GA).
- This should be queue-based to avoid thundering herds.

4) Optional extended backfill (by request)
- Run in off-peak hours; enforce a maximum warehouse spend per run; throttle to N workspaces/day.

Implementation details (warehouse)
- Partition by date (day) + cluster/sort by workspace_id, route_template, model_bucket.
- Backfill job reads raw events with predicate pushdown on event_date partitions.
- Use a “route_template_quality” field (good/unknown) to track normalization success; keep unknown grouped under a safe bucket instead of exploding cardinality.

Idempotency rules
- For any partition/day, backfill recompute must overwrite the entire partition (or deterministically merge) to avoid duplicate rows from reruns.
- Export/billing reconciliation queries must read the same snapshot as the console (avoid mixing partially recomputed partitions).

Versioning & historical drift controls
We need to decide whether changing normalization/bucketing logic retroactively rewrites history.
- Beta: freeze normalization + model bucketing version per workspace once enabled.
- GA: allow upgrades but treat as a “data revision” event and show a note in internal logs; do not silently rewrite without a planned backfill.
- Store normalization_version and model_bucket_version on aggregate rows for internal debugging (not necessarily exposed to customers).

Correctness & reconciliation plan
Goal
- Aggregated totals should match billing totals within tolerance for the same workspace/time range, accounting for:
  - rounding (currency conversion + per-token rounding)
  - timing boundaries (timezone) and late events
  - excluded traffic (e.g., free tier credits, internal test workspaces)

Checks
- Daily automated check for allowlisted workspaces:
  - Compare sum(cost_usd) from aggregate vs billing ledger for day D.
  - Flag drift > max(1.0 USD, 0.5%) (initial beta thresholds; adjust as we learn).
- Dimension completeness metrics:
  - % events missing route tag
  - % events missing model id/bucket
  - % events assigned to “unknown_route” bucket
- “What changed” safety check:
  - If a week-over-week delta is driven primarily by missing-dim changes (e.g., route tag missing rate jumped), do NOT generate a top-driver explanation; show “Data quality issue detected” instead.

Expected failure modes (and how we handle them)
- Missing route tags in older data: totals may still be correct, but breakdown is skewed; mitigate by bucketing into “Unattributed route” and showing a warning banner.
- Model alias duplication: two model identifiers that map to same bucket can create duplicate rows if bucketing changes mid-window; fix by enforcing stable bucketing version and rerunning affected partitions.
- Timeouts on long ranges: even with aggregates, 90-day queries can be heavy; mitigate by requiring exports for long ranges and limiting interactive range (UI guardrail + API guardrail).

Customer expectations & messaging (beta)
What we will claim
- Usage Insights shows route + model cost breakdown for the last ~14 days after enablement.
- Data may be delayed by up to 2–3 hours (banner will show freshness timestamp).
- Totals are expected to match invoices, but there can be small timing/rounding deltas; we’ll provide a “billing reconciliation” note.

What we will NOT claim in beta
- “All historical costs are available.”
- “Breakdown is guaranteed to be complete for all routes/models for all time ranges.”

Console UX expectations (must-have)
- Time range picker should not default to a range beyond backfill coverage for that workspace.
- If a user selects a range with partial coverage:
  - show “Partial data” banner (include earliest available timestamp)
  - keep totals consistent (do not display 0 rows without explanation)
- For “Unattributed route” bucket:
  - tooltip: explains missing route tags / unnormalized paths
  - link to docs/troubleshooting and recommended instrumentation checks

Support / customer success guidance
- We should maintain a short internal checklist for “customer asks for older history”:
  1) verify workspace is on beta allowlist
  2) check raw event retention window + missing-dim rates
  3) if acceptable, run extended backfill for that workspace (and communicate that historical data may be less complete)
  4) if not acceptable, offer export from billing totals and set expectation for GA

Rollout plan & owners
- Phase 0/1 (beta enablement):
  - Nadia + Logan: implement backfill bootstrap job + throttling
  - Allison + Caleb: add dashboard panels for missing route/model dims and drift
  - Cole: confirm reconciliation tolerances + ledger query source of truth
  - Chloe/Dylan: ensure console shows earliest available timestamp and partial banners

- Phase 2 (expand window to 30 days):
  - Gate on: (a) drift < thresholds, (b) missing route tags < 0.5% for hosted, (c) no critical incidents from backfill runs for 2 weeks.

Operational considerations
- Warehouse spend guardrails:
  - cap backfill jobs to X partitions/hour; abort if estimated scan exceeds threshold
  - run off-peak UTC
- Queueing:
  - use a job queue keyed by workspace_id; dedupe repeated requests; include cancellation
- Observability:
  - emit job metrics: rows processed, partitions overwritten, duration, scan bytes, success/failure
  - alert if backfill job failure rate > 5% in 1h or if scan bytes spike > 2x baseline

Open questions
1) What is the true raw metering event retention by deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private)? Need confirmation from Security/Compliance and actual TTLs.
2) Do we allow customers to request a backfill beyond standard retention if data is in cold storage? (Probably no for beta; consider enterprise paid add-on later.)
3) Do we want to persist aggregates longer than raw events? This helps console performance but complicates “recompute after logic change.”
4) For Private deployments: do we support any backfill in initial beta, or do we require customer to run a local job? (Likely defer; document as limitation.)

Next steps (this week)
- Nadia/Logan: write the one-time backfill bootstrap job spec (inputs, throttles, overwrite semantics) and align with ENG-3812 implementation.
- Cole: provide updated reconciliation tolerance proposal for 14d and 30d ranges.
- Allison/Caleb: draft dashboard + alert thresholds for missing dimensions and drift (tie into usage-insights-data-freshness-and-quality).
- Chloe/Dylan: ensure UI includes earliest coverage and partial-data banner copy before enabling more beta accounts.
